Last month, after the television tracking app TV Time officially shut down, one of its co-founders, Antonio Pinto, announced the launch of a brand-new TV and movie tracking app called Bingers, which will place greater emphasis on social features. Here are the details.

Bingers is now available for download

When Whip Media announced the closure of TV Time, one of its co-founders immediately announced the launch of Bingers, positioned as "a fast and beautiful wishlist paired with a fun community".

Now, as first reported by TechCrunch, Bingers is available for download on iOS and Android, offering a kind of spiritual continuation for users who have been unable to find a replacement — after all, TV Time was once one of the most widely used TV tracking apps in the world.

Former users who used the platform's export tool to save their data before TV Time shut down can import their archives into Bingers for a seamless transition; users who never exported their data, or who are using a TV tracking app for the first time, can start building their records from scratch.

Bingers significantly enhances its community-driven features, including user profiles, comments, show ratings, GIFs, polls, and character popularity matchups. Pinto told TechCrunch that these are precisely the key elements that made TV Time so beloved by users over the years:

For users who simply want to track the TV shows and movies they've watched, Bingers offers standalone wishlist and viewing history features. Similar to TV Time, the app also displays a calendar of upcoming and premiering shows, with a countdown showing how many days until each premiere.

Bingers is available for free download on the App Store, with no in-app purchases at present.
